questions.q: $|x| < 1$, the coefficient of $x^3$ in the expansion of $\log  \left(1+x+x^2\right)$ in ascending powers of $x, is$
questions.solution:
We have,
$\log \left(1+x+x^2\right)=\log \frac{\left(1-x^3\right)}{(1-x)}\begin{aligned} & =\log \left(1-x^3\right)-\log (1-x) \\ & =-\left[x^3+\frac{x^6}{2}+\frac{x^9}{3}+\ldots\right]+\left[x+\frac{x^2}{2}+\frac{x^3}{3}+\ldots\right] \\ & \text { Coefficient of } x^3=-1+\frac{1}{3}=-\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\frac{x-4}{x^2-5 x+6}$ can be expanded in the ascending powers of $x$, then the coefficient of $x^3$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{x-4}{x^2-5 x+6}=\frac{x-4}{(x-2)(x-3)} \\ & =\frac{2}{(x-2)}-\frac{1}{(x-3)}=2(x-2)^{-1}-(x-3)^{-1} \\ & =2(-2)^{-1}\left(1-\frac{x}{2}\right)^{-1}-(-3)^{-1}\left(1-\frac{x}{3}\right)^{-1} \\ & =-\left[1+\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^3+\ldots\right] \\ & \quad+\frac{1}{3}\left[1+\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)+\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)^2+\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)^3+\ldots\right] \\ & \therefore \text { Coefficient of } x^3 \text { in } \frac{x-4}{x^2-5 x+6} .\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3+\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^3 \\ & =-\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{81}=\frac{-81+8}{648} \\ & =-\frac{73}{648}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The coefficient of $x^k$ in the expansion of $\frac{1-2 x-x^2}{e^{-x}}$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Now, } \frac{1-2 x-x^2}{e^{-x}} \\ & =\left(1-2 x-x^2\right)\left(e^x\right) \\ & =\left(1-2 x-x^2\right)\left(1+x+\frac{x^2}{2 !}+\frac{x^3}{3 !}+\ldots\right. \\ & \left.+\frac{x^k}{k !}+\ldots \infty\right) \\ & =\left(1+x+\frac{x^2}{2 !}+\ldots+\frac{x^k}{k !}+\ldots \infty\right)-2\left(x+x^2+\frac{x^3}{2 !}\right. \\ & \left.+\ldots+\frac{x^k}{(k-1) !}+\frac{x^{k+1}}{k !}+\ldots \infty\right) \\ & -\left(x^2+x^3+\frac{x^4}{2 !}+\ldots .\right. \\ & \left.\frac{x^k}{(k-2) !}+\frac{x^{k+1}}{(k-1) !}+\frac{x^{k+2}}{k !}+\ldots \infty\right) \\ & \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \text { Coefficient of } x^k \text { in }\left(\frac{1-2 x-x^2}{e^{-x}}\right) \\ &=\frac{1}{k !}-\frac{2}{(k-1) !}-\frac{1}{(k-2) !} \\ &=\frac{1}{k !}-\frac{2 k}{k(k-1) !}-\frac{k(k-1)}{k(k-1)(k-2) !} \\ &=\frac{1}{k !}-\frac{2 k}{k !}-\frac{k(k-1)}{k !} \\ &=\frac{1-k-k^2}{k !}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If ${5}^{97}$ is divided by $52$, then the remainder obtained is
questions.solution:
We know that, ${5}^{4} = 625 = 52 \times 12 + 1$

$⇒ {5}^{4} = 52\lambda + 1$ , where $\lambda$ is a positive integer.

$⇒ {\left({5}^{4}\right)}^{24} = {\left(52\lambda + 1\right)}^{24}$

$= {C}_{0} 24 {\left(52\lambda\right)}^{24} + {C}_{1}{\left(52\lambda\right)}^{23} + {C}_{2} 24 {\left(52\lambda\right)}^{22} 24 + \ldots + {C}_{23}\left(52\lambda\right) + {C}_{24} 24 24$ (by binomial theorem)

$⇒ {5}^{96} = 52\left[{C}_{0} 24 {52}^{23}{\lambda}^{24} + {C}_{1}{52}^{23}{\lambda}^{22} 24 + \ldots + {C}_{23}\lambda 24\right] + 1$

$= \left(amultipleof52\right) + 1$

On multiplying both sides by $5$ , we get

${5}^{97} = {5}^{96} ⋅ 5 = 5\left(amultipleof52\right) + 5$

Hence, the required remainder is $5$ .

questions.q: If ${ }^{n-3} C_r+B^{n-3} C_{r-1}+B^{\prime n-3} C_{r-2}+\binom{n-3}{r-3}={ }^n C_r$ holds. for all $n \geq r \geq 3$, then \left(B \cdot B^{\prime}\right)=$.$
questions.solution: ${ }^{n-3} C_r+B^{n-3} C_{r-1}+B^{\prime n-3} C_{r-2}+\binom{n-3}{r-3}={ }^n C_r\Rightarrow\left({ }^{n-3} C_r+\binom{n-3}{r-1}\right)+\left(\binom{n-3}{r-1}+\binom{n-3}{r-2}\right)+\left(\binom{n-3}{r-2}+\binom{n-3}{r-3}\right)+(B-2)\binom{n-3}{r-1}+\left(B^{\prime}-2\right)\binom{n-3}{r-2}={ }^n C_3\Rightarrow\left[{ }^{n-2} C_r+\binom{n-2}{r-1}\right]+\binom{n-2}{r-2}+\left(\binom{n-3}{r-1}+\binom{n-3}{r-2}\right)+(B-3)\binom{n-3}{r-1}+\left(B^{\prime}-3\right)\binom{n-3}{r-2}={ }^n C_r\Rightarrow{ }^{n-1} C_r+\left[\binom{n-2}{r-2}+\binom{n-2}{r-1}\right]+(B-3)^{n-3} C_{r-2}+\left(B^{\prime}-3\right)\binom{n-3}{r-2}={ }^n C_r\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow{ }^n C_r+(B-3)\binom{n-3}{r-1}+\left(B^{\prime}-3\right)^{n-3} C_{r-2}={ }^n C_r \\ & \Rightarrow(B-3)\binom{n-3}{r-1}+\left(B^{\prime}-3\right)\binom{n-3}{r-2}=0\end{aligned}$ It is only possible when, $B-3=0$ and $B^{\prime}-3=0\therefore\left(B, B^{\prime}\right) \equiv(3,3)$

questions.q: If the middle term in the binomial expansion of ${\left(\dfrac{1}{x} + xsinx\right)}^{10}$ is $\dfrac{63}{8},$ then the value of $6\sin^{2}x + sinx - 2$ is
questions.solution:
Here, $n = 10,$ which is even.
Middle term $= {\left(\dfrac{10}{2} + 1\right)}^{th}$ term $= {6}^{th}$ term
${\text{T}}_{6} = {}^{10} {\text{C}}_{5} {\left(\dfrac{1}{\text{x}}\right)}^{5} {( \text{x}sin\text{x} )}^{5}$
$⇒ \dfrac{63}{8} = 252{\left(sinx\right)}^{5}$
$⇒ {\left(sinx\right)}^{5} = \dfrac{1}{32}$
$⇒ {\left(sinx\right)}^{5} = {\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{5}$
$⇒ sinx = \dfrac{1}{2}$
$⇒ 2sinx - 1 = 0$
$⇒ 6\sin^{2}x + sinx - 2 = \left(2sinx - 1\right)\left(3sinx + 2\right) = 0$

questions.q: The number of rational terms in the expansion of \left(3\dfrac{1}{4} + 7\dfrac{1}{6}\right)144$ is$
questions.solution:
Let,

$S = \left(3\dfrac{1}{4} + 7\dfrac{1}{6}\right)144$

General term of~$S$~is given by

${T}_{r + 1} = Cr 144 \left\{\left(3\right)\dfrac{144 - r}{4}\right\}\left\{\left(7\right)\dfrac{r}{6}\right\}$

Now, for the rational terms

\left(\dfrac{144 - r}{4}\right) \in W \left(\text{whole number}\right)

For this~$r$~must be the multiple of~$4$~therefore

$r = 0, 4, 8, . . . , 140, 144$

And,

\left(\dfrac{r}{6}\right) \inW \left(\text{whole number}\right)

For this~$r$~must be the multiple of~$6$~therefore

$r = 0, 6, 12, 18, 24, . . . . . , 138, 144$

Now, common terms are

$0, 12, 24, . . . . , 144$

This is an AP. So,

$144 = 0 + \left($n - 1\right)12$

$⇒ n = 13$.

$

questions.q: The sum of all the coefficients in the binomial expansion of \((1+2 x)^n\) is 6561. Let \(R=(I+2 x)^n=I+F\), where \(I \in N\) and \(0 < F < $\mathrm{l}$\). If \(x=$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$\), then \(1-$\frac{F}{1+(\sqrt{2}-1)^4}=$\)
questions.solution: It is given that sum of all the coefficients in the binomial expansion of \((1+2 x)^n\) is \(6561=(1+2)^n\) on putting \(x=1\). \(\begin{array}{ll} \Rightarrow & 3^n=6561 \\ \Rightarrow & n=8 \end{array}\) Now, at \$(x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$\), then \(R=(1+2 x)^n=I+F\) \(\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow $R=(\sqrt{2}+$1)^8=I+F, $\text { where }$I \in N $\text { and }$0 < F < 1 \\ & \$therefore(\sqrt{2}-$1)^8=F^{\prime}, $\text { where }$0 < F^{\prime} < 1 \\ & \$therefore(\s$sqrt{2}+1)^8+(\s$sqrt{2}-1)^8=I+\left($F+F^{\prime}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow $2\left[(\sqrt{2})^8+{ }^8 $C_2(\sqrt{2})^6+{ }^8 $C_4(\sqrt{2})^4+{ }^8 $C_6(\sqrt{2})^2+{ }^8 C_8\right] \\ & \$quad=I+\left($F+F^{\prime}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow $\text { Even integer }}=I+\left($F+F^{\prime}\right) \\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow F+F^{\prime} \in $\text { Integer }$\\ \text{ and } \because 0 < F < 1 $\text { and }$0 < F^{\prime} < 1 \Rightarrow 0 < F+F^{\prime} < 2 \\ \text{ and } $\text { So, }$F+F^{\prime}=1 \\ \text{ and } \Rightarrow F=1-F^{\$prime}=1-(\sqrt{2}-1)^8 \end{aligned}\) \(\begin{aligned} & $\text { So, }1-\frac{F}{1+(\s$sqrt{2}-1)^4}=1-\f$frac{1-(\sqrt{2}-1)^8}{1+(\sqrt{2}-1)^4}$\\ \text{ and } $=1-\frac{\left[1+(\sqrt{2}-1)^4\right]\left[1-(\sqrt{2}-1)^4\right]}{1+(\sqrt{2}-1)^4}$\\ \text{ and } $=1-\l$left[1-(\sqrt{2}-$1)^4\$right]=(\sqrt{2}-$1)^4 \end{aligned}\) Hence, option (3) is correct.

questions.q: The first negative coefficient in the terms occurring in the expansion of $( 1 + x) \dfrac{21}{5}$ is
questions.solution:
The expansion of \left(1 + x\right)\dfrac{21}{5} = 1 + \dfrac{21}{5}x + \dfrac{\dfrac{21}{5}\left(\dfrac{21}{5} - 1\right)}{2 !}x^{2} + \dfrac{\dfrac{21}{5}\left(\dfrac{21}{5} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{21}{5} - 2\right)}{3 !}x^{3} + \ldots$

Simplify the above expansion.

\left(1 + x\right)\dfrac{21}{5} = 1 + \dfrac{21}{5}x + \dfrac{21 \times 16}{{5}^{2} \times 2 !}x^{2} + \dfrac{21 \times 16 \times 11}{{5}^{3} \times 3 !}x^{3} + \dfrac{21 \times 16 \times 11 \times 6}{{5}^{4} \times 4 !} + . .$

The first negative coefficient in the terms occurring in the~expansion of $( 1 + x) \dfrac{21}{5}$ is

$= - \dfrac{21 \times 16 \times 11 \times 6 \times 1 \times 4}{{5}^{6} \times 6 !}$

$= \dfrac{- 88704}{{5}^{7} \times 144}$

$= \dfrac{- 616}{57}$

$= n{C}_{r}a^{r}x^{- \dfrac{3}{4}n + \dfrac{3}{4}r + \dfrac{5}{4}r}$

$r = \dfrac{n\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)}{\dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{5}{4}}$

$∴ r = \dfrac{3n}{8}$

The term independent of $x$ is $448$.

$⇒ C\dfrac{3n}{8} n a\dfrac{3n}{8} = 448$

Sum of coefficient between $200$ and $400$ is given as

$200 < \left(1 + a\right)n < 400$

According to the question,
${}^{n}{C}_{r}a^{r}$ = 448
$⇒{}^{8}{C}_{3}a^{3} = 448$
$⇒56a^{3} = 448$
$⇒a^{3} = 8$~
$⇒a = 2$

$⇒n = 8, a = 2$

questions.q: For $|x| < \frac{1}{2}$, if the coefficient of $x^{10}$ and the constant term in the expansion of $\frac{2 x^3+8 x^2-2 x-2}{(1-x)(1+x)(1-2 x)}$ in powers of $x$ are $l$ and $m$ respectively, then $1 m=$
questions.solution: The given expression is $\frac{2 x^3+8 x^2-2 x-2}{(1-x)(1+x)(1-2 x)}=\frac{2 x^3+8 x^2-2 x-2}{(2 x-1)(x-1)(x+1)}=1+\frac{A}{2 x-1}+\frac{B}{x-1}+\frac{C}{x+1}$ (By partial fraction) $\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow 2 x^3+8 x^2-2 x & -2 \\ =\left(2 x^3\right. & \left.-x^2-2 x+1\right)+A\left(x^2-1\right) \\ & +B\left(2 x^2+x-1\right)+C\left(2 x^2-3 x+1\right)\end{aligned}$ On comparing, we get $\begin{aligned}-1+A+2 B+2 C & =8 \\ -2+B-3 C & =-2\end{aligned}$ and $\quad 1-A-B+C=-2$ On solving we have $A=1, B=3$ and $C=1\therefore$ Given expression is $\begin{aligned} & \frac{2 x^3+8 x^2-2 x-2}{(1-x)(1+x)(1-2 x)}=1-\frac{1}{1-2 x}-\frac{3}{1-x}+\frac{1}{1+x} \\ = & 1-(1-2 x)^{-1}-3(1-x)^{-1}+(1+x)^{-1}\end{aligned}\therefore$ Coefficient of $x^{10}$ is $-2^{10}-3+1=-2-2^{10}=l$ and constant term is $1-1-3+1=-2=m\therefore \quad l m=4  \left(1+2^9\right)$

questions.q: The greatest integer which divides the number ${101}^{100} - 1$ is
questions.solution:
For the greatest integer which divides the number 101100 - 1, consider

${\left(1 + \text{x}\right)}^{n} = \left(1 + \text{nx} + $\dfrac{\text{n} \left(\text{n} - 1\right)}{2}$x^{2} + \text{........} +x^{n}\right)$

{by Binomial theorem)

$⇒ ${ \left($1 + $\text{x}\right)}^{n} - 1 = $\text{nx} + \dfrac{\left(\text{n} - 1\right)}{2}$x^{2} + $\text{........} +$x^{n}$

If $x = n$, then;

{ \left(1 + \text{n}\right)}^{n} - 1 = n^{2} + \dfrac{\text{n} \left(\text{n} - 1\right)}${2}$n^{2} + \text{...} +n^{n}$

$⇒ {\left($1 + $\text{n}\right)}^{n} - 1 = n^{2} \left[$1 + \dfrac{\text{n} \left(\text{n} -1\right)}{2} +\text{...}n^{\text{n} -$2}\right]$

Put $n = 100$ in the equation,

${\left($1 + 1 0 0\right)}^{1 0 0} - 1 = 1 0 {0}^{2} \left[1 + $\dfrac{1 0 0 \left(1 0 0 - 1\right)}${2} + \text{........} +1 0 {0}^{9 8}\right]$

$⇒ \left(101\right)100 - 1 = 10{0}^{2}\left[1 + $\dfrac{100 \times 99}{2} + \text{...} +$10{0}^{98}\right] ⇒ \left(101\right)100 - 1 = {100}^{2} \left(m\right)$

Clearly, ${101}^{100} - 1$ is divisible by ${100}^{2}$.$

questions.q: If $n$ is an even positive integer greater than $1$ and $x > 0$, then the condition that the greatest term in the expansion of \left(1 + x\right)n$ may have the greatest coefficient also is$
questions.solution:
If $n$ is even, the greatest coefficient is ${}^{n}{C}_{n / 2}$

$∴$ The greatest term $= {}^{n}{C}_{n / 2}x^{n / 2}$

$∴ {}^{n}{C}_{n / 2}x^{n / 2} > {}^{n}{C}_{\left(n / 2\right) - 1}x^{\left(n / 2\right) - 1}$

and ${}^{n}{C}_{n / 2}x^{n / 2} > {}^{n}{C}_{\left(n / 2\right) + 1}x^{\left(n / 2\right) + 1}$

$⇒\dfrac{n - \dfrac{n}{2} + 1}{n2}x > 1$

and $\dfrac{n - \left(\dfrac{n}{2} + 1\right) + 1}{\dfrac{n}{2} + 1}x < 1$

$⇒ \left(n / 2\right)\left(n / 2\right) + 1 < \text{x} < \left(\dfrac{n}{2} + 1\right)\dfrac{n}{2}$

Hence, $\dfrac{n}{n + 2} < x < \dfrac{n + 2}{n}$

questions.q: A possible value of ' $x$ ', for which the ninth term in the expansion of \left\{{3}^{\log_{3}\sqrt{{25}^{x - 1} + 7}} + {3}^{\left(- \dfrac{1}{8}\right)\log_{3}\left({5}^{x - 1} + 1\right)}\right\}10$ in the increasing powers of ${3}^{\left(- \dfrac{1}{8}\right)\log_{3}\left({5}^{x - 1} + 1\right)}$ is equal to~$180$, is :$
questions.solution:
\left\{{3}^{\log_{3}\sqrt{{25}^{x - 1} + 7}} + {3}^{\left(- \dfrac{1}{8}\right)\log_{3}\left({5}^{x - 1} + 1\right)}\right\}10$

$= \left\{\sqrt{{25}^{x - 1} + 7} + \left({5}^{x - 1} + 1\right)\dfrac{- 1}{8}\right\}10$, using~$a^{n\log_{\mathrm{a}}x} = x^{n}$

Using the formula of the general term in the Binomial theorem for non negative integral index, i.e.,~${T}_{r + 1} = Cr n a^{n - r}b^{r}$~in~\left(a + b\right)n$, we get,~

$C8 10 \left({25}^{( x - 1 )} + 7\right) \times \left({5}^{( x - 1 )} + 1\right)- 1 = 180$

$⇒ \dfrac{{25}^{x - 1} + 7}{{5}^{( x - 1 )} + 1} = 4$

$⇒ \dfrac{t^{2} + 7}{t + 1} = 4$, taking~$t = {5}^{x - 1}$

$⇒ t = 1, 3 ⇒ {5}^{x - 1} = 1 ⇒ {5}^{x - 1} = {5}^{0}$

$⇒ x - 1 = 0$~(one of the possible value).

$⇒ x = 1$

questions.q: Consider the following statements I : The number of non-trivial even divisors of the number \(2^{\alpha_1} 3^{\alpha_2} 4^{\alpha_3} 5^{\alpha_4} 6^{\alpha_5}\), is \(\left(\alpha_1+1\right)\left(\alpha_2+1\right)\left(\alpha_3+1\right)\left(\alpha_4+1\right)\left(\alpha_5+1\right)-2\) II : The number of non-trivial odd divisors of the number \(2^{\alpha_1} $\cdot$3^{\alpha_2} $\cdot$4^{\alpha_3} $\cdot$5^{\alpha_4} $\cdot$6^{\alpha_5}\), is \(\alpha_2+\alpha_4+\alpha_5+\alpha_2 \alpha_4+\alpha_4 \alpha_5\). Then
options: I is false and II is false
I is true and II is true
I is false and II is true
I is true and II is false
questions.solution: Given number \(=2^{\alpha_1} 3^{\alpha_2} 4^{\alpha_3} 5^{\alpha_4} 6^{\alpha_5}\) \(=2^{\alpha_1+2 \alpha_3+\alpha_5 3^{\alpha_2}+\alpha_5 5^{\alpha_4}}\) Number of non-trivial even divisors \$(=\left(\alpha_1+2 \alpha_3+\alpha_5\$right)\left(\alpha_2+\alpha_5+1\$right)\left(\alpha_4+1\right)-1\) And, number of non-trivial odd divisors \(\begin{aligned} & $=\left(\alpha_2+\alpha_5+1\$right)\left(\alpha_4+1\right)-1 \\  \text{ and }  =\alpha_2+\alpha_4+\alpha_5+\alpha_2 \alpha_4+\alpha_4 \alpha_5+1-1 \end{aligned}\) \(\therefore\) Statement \$(\mathrm{I}$\) is false and \$(\mathrm{II}\) is true.

questions.q: The coefficients of \(x^{50}\) in \((1+x)^{101}\) \(\left($1-x+x²\right)^{100}\) is......$
questions.solution: Given expression is \(\begin{aligned} & $(1+x)^{101}\left($1-x+x^2\right)^{100} \\ & $=(1+x)\l$left[(1+x)\left($1-x+x^2\right)\right]^{100} \\ \text{ and } $=(1+x)\left($1+x^3\right)^{100} \end{aligned}\) So, coefficient of \(x^{50}\) in \$((1+x)^{101}\left($1-x+x^2\right)^{100}\) \(=\) coefficient of \(x^{50}\) in \$((1+x)\left($1+x^3\right)^{100}\) \(=\) coefficient of \(x^{50}\) in \$(\left($1+x^3\right)^{100}\) + coefficient of \(x^{49}\) in \$(\left($1+x^3\right)^{100}\) \(\because\) In the expansion of \$(\left($1+x^3\right)^{100}\), the power of \(x\) is multiple of 3 , and while 50 and 49 are not multiple of 3. So, coefficient of \(x^{50}\) and 49 in the expansion of \$(\left($1+x^3\right)^{100}\) is zero. \(\therefore\) Coefficient of \(x^{50}\) in \$((1+x)^{100}\left($1-x+x^2\right)^{101}\) is zero. Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.q: Let $x \in \mathbf{R}$ be so small that the powers of $x$ beyond two are insignificant and negligibly small. For such $x$, if $(1-x)^3(2+x)^6$ is approximated by $a+b x+c x^2$, then $a+b+c=$
questions.solution: We have, $\begin{gathered} (1-x)^3=1-3 x+3 x^2 \text { [neglecting higher term] } \\ \begin{array}{c} (2+x)^6={ }^6 C_0 2^6 x^0+{ }^6 C_1 2^5 x^1+{ }^6 C_2 2^4 x^2 \\ \text { [neglecting higher term] } \end{array} \\ =64+192 x+240 x^2 \end{gathered}$ [neglecting higher term] $=64+192 x+240 x^2$ Now, $\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &(1-x)^3(2+x)^6=\left(1-3 x+3 x^2\right)\left(64+192 x+240 x^2\right) \\ &= 64+192 x+240 x^2-192 x-576 x^2+192 x^2 \\ & \quad \text { (neglecting higher term) } \\ &=-144 x^2+64 \\ & \therefore \quad a=64, b=0, c=-144 \\ & \therefore a+b+c=64+0-144=-80 \end{aligned} \end{aligned}$
